name: FAST (Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope)
description: A 500-metre single-dish radio telescope built in a natural depression in Guizhou, with an active surface of 4,500 metal panels that forms a movable parabolic shape. It observes radio wavelengths from 10 cm to 4.3 m.
highlights: Construction began in 2011 and first light came in September 2016; it was fully operational on 11 January 2020.
Its first discoveries were two pulsars, PSR J1859-01 and PSR J1931-02, in August 2017.
By November 2024 it had found over 1,000 pulsars.
